findings.mechanism_confirmed: OpenShell injects provider creds as opaque placeholders (openshell:resolve:env:v<rev>_<key>) into sandbox env under GENERIC names (api_key, access_token, refresh_token, account_id) — NOT SDK-conventional names (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY etc.). Real values never touch sandbox disk; proxy substitutes at L7.
findings.codex_RESOLVED: access_token placeholder -> api.openai.com returned token_expired (real OAuth credential reached OpenAI). PROVES placeholder->L7-substitution->real-credential path works end-to-end.
findings.codex_caveat: access token is EXPIRED; no refresh configured (refresh status: none). Needs OAuth refresh wiring.
findings.anthropic_ANOMALY: api_key placeholder NOT rewritten (401 invalid x-api-key = placeholder reached Anthropic verbatim). Reproduced across claude-code profile AND custom anthropic-api profile, in both x-api-key and Authorization:Bearer headers. Codex (same revision, same sandbox) resolves. Root cause not yet found.
findings.bedrock_WITHHELD: gateway log: 'withholding static provider credential handle from endpointless profile' — aws-bedrock profile is declarative-only (bridge-fronted), injects nothing by design.
findings.consumption_path_gap: prime-agent reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / CODEX_AUTH_* from env, but OpenShell injects generic names (api_key/access_token). A mapping bridge (export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=$api_key) is required. Env precedence in prime-agent not yet confirmed.
findings.operational_hazard: docker restart on the sandbox container wedges the gateway phase at Error (supervisor re-registration does not clear it); recovery = delete+recreate. Gateway active-pointer flips (nemoclaw<->openshell) caused earlier churn; now pinned to openshell.

status: IN_PROGRESS — anthropic resolution anomaly is the open blocker for a clean GO
